attempts.text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"The commitment to being a multi-tendency organization, rooted in the core values and politics put forth in the DSA Constitution, guides the work of DSA.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The current underlying tendency within DSA towards winner-take-all politics, hateful rhetoric, and personal attacks is undermining the most important task of DSA: building organized power for the working class.", "claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA needs well thought out rules for managing internal disagreements.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA should require adoption of codes of conduct and standards for managing internal disagreement at every level of the organization, including organizing committees, chapters, working groups, and the National Political Committee.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Different factions in DSA can provide important representation of different political views and strategies, while working to improve DSA as an organization.", "claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Factions in DSA should not put the interest of the caucus above the interest of DSA as a whole.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Factions in DSA should not put the interest of the caucus above the interest of the movement as a whole.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
